input.query: ROE-5.1 ROE-5.2 ROE-5.3 jammer

new_information.info: Patrol 2 has eyes on at the beach (08:21:30, 10 s old). About 5 walkers are near (-1800,-60). One is holding a drone controller and watching a tablet. The drone is visible over the water just off the beach, and no boats are offshore. This confirms the pilot is on base, within about 30 m of the RF pilot fix (-1822,-48). Security is already at the pilot, so rung 2 can be carried out now. The pilot is among other people, so a drone that loses its link and returns to the pilot, or falls, would come down over the group on the beach (ROE-5.3). The report also matches the track, so PVID is held, but this does not matter for the jammer.

input.pvid_status: Not required for the jammer. For reference, the control room has PVID: S-GIM 08:21:40 shows a quadcopter with blade spin (conf 0.85), and Patrol 2 (C-04, 08:21:30) saw the drone over the water off the beach. Both match the track.
input.override_assessment: Operator's reason: the drone has circled off the beach for over a minute, and the operator wants it brought down before it moves over the base. Reviewer's reasons: threat is MEDIUM; rung 2 (security to the pilot, ROE-6.1) is the lowest rung likely to work and has not been tried (ROE-1.5); the jammer is not cleared because the tower check is pending (ROE-5.2); and a stronger response is not justified with the pilot on base. My weighing: the operator's concern is reasonable, but it is speculative. The drone has been orbiting over water since 08:20:00, and the base is about 1.7 km from the nearest critical asset (Z-HOUSE, 1690 m). Rung 3 is allowed at MEDIUM (ROE-4.1), but it still needs the ROE-5.2 clearance and the least-force test (ROE-1.5), and neither is met. C-04 strengthens the reviewer's side, because the pilot is identified and a patrol is next to him. I side with the reviewer.
input.concerns: 1) ROE-5.2: no tower statement on crewed aircraft is available. The track is inside the Z-APPR outline, and N-12 says Z-APPR is used only when the tower reports an arrival or departure. The line of fire lists Z-APPR as never-backstop when aircraft are active. Control-room info has no air-traffic entry. The jammer cannot be cleared until the tower confirms no crewed aircraft within 3 km. Other ROE-5.2 check: Z-SHIP is 3510 m from the target, and C-04 reports no boats offshore, so the vessel limit is not an issue. 2) ROE-1.5: security has not yet tried the pilot. A patrol is already at the beach with eyes on the controller holder. 3) ROE-5.3: link loss could make the drone return to the pilot among about 5 people, hover, or land or fall in the water. Behaviour on link loss is unknown. 4) Weather is unavailable (visibility and wind unknown). This matters less for the jammer than for the laser and interceptor, but it is another unknown. 5) The track is moving away from the base: it is over water and not heading for a critical asset. Re-check the distance to Z-HOUSE each cycle and escalate if it heads to the housing or other assets. 6) The S-RF altitude readings are erratic (-72 to 122 m) against radar at 55-69 m. S-RF position and heading do agree with the other sensors, so treat RF altitude as unreliable. S-ACO is degraded (H-03). 7) If the pilot is confirmed and cooperative, ask for a landing. Only if security fails or the drone nears a critical asset, and only after the tower confirms no aircraft within 3 km, would rung 3 be worth re-requesting. Pair it with the security contact.
input.safer_alternative: Rung 2, now. Direct Patrol 2 to the walker holding the controller near (-1800,-60). Detain and question him, and have him land the drone (ROE-6.1). Keep the other walkers clear. In parallel, ask the tower whether Z-APPR is active and whether any crewed aircraft is within 3 km (N-12, ROE-5.2). Keep S-GIM and radar on T-1. Brief the watch supervisor (ROE-6.5). Keep the jammer available only if security fails or the drone heads toward the base.

The jammer needs the tower's confirmation of no crewed aircraft within 3 km first. The interceptor and laser need HIGH. The laser is also blocked by its beam path, which crosses Z-APPR, a Never-backstop zone. The gun needs CRITICAL.
